answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day expiration create a forcing function, but the 94% line utilization makes delivery risk the binding constraint. Switching to the low-cost vendor (c2) is ruled out: they missed SLA in 3/4 quarters and cannot be sole source for a critical line. Renewing at status quo (c1) forgoes cost reduction. Adding a second source lacks time and definition. Deferral (c5) worked for non-critical items but this is primary supply. The highest-leverage move is aggressive negotiation (c4): benchmarking recovered real margin before, and the incumbent has already locked in multi-year volume pricing (c6), meaning they have room to improve terms without losing economics. Verify c2 to confirm SLA risk quantitatively and c4 to understand the scope of prior margin recovery, then negotiate hard on unit price and payment terms to hit the 18% target while keeping the proven, low-risk incumbent in place. This preserves delivery stability on the 94% line while forcing a margin conversation.
